description: I'm Sidak Mann, a Brophy sophomore and founder of Strygonia, building BlackBox, a systems debugging device. I've built GhostLink (encrypted messaging), RomExplorer (Android), a Fortran compiler, and wheresmywater.org (featured on ABC15, 6,000+ visitors). I code in C++, TypeScript, HTML, and Python, and know AI. Seeking: data analysis, ML, visualization, UI/UX, space medicine, writing. Beginners welcome.
summary:
Vigil is an offline health monitor for long space missions. It learns each crew member's own normal from the first ten days of readings, then watches heart, immune, bone and muscle, behavior and radiation data for slow drift. It combines small changes across many signals into one score, explains each alert in plain words with the numbers behind it, and decides the level: handle it on board, tell the Medical Officer, or send a priority packet to Earth.

It runs as native desktop software on macOS and Linux, with no network connections. Each person signs in with a PIN, sees only their own raw data, and chooses what to share. Readings come from daily check-ins, manual entry, Apple Health exports or spreadsheets. 
To make interacting more enjoyable, Vigil adds an organ group chat, texts from future you, a lab results ticker, an immune replay, a heart rate album and Gut City.
details: Vigil is an offline health monitor for astronauts on long missions, built by The Trojans. It learns each crew member’s own normal and spots slow drift in heart, immune, bone and muscle, behavior and radiation readings, explaining every change in plain words and deciding whether to handle it on board, tell the Medical Officer, or call Earth across a 22-minute delay. A clickable body map ties every reading to NASA’s five hazards of human spaceflight (radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields, and hostile closed environments) and to the risks named by NASA’s Human Research Program, with simple steps for how to measure, why it matters, and what to do. Blood sugar is judged against CDC ranges, and cabin CO2 and radiation dose against NASA-STD-3001 limits. Real NASA DONKI data on 167 solar storms from 2010 to 2026 shows the Sun’s cycle on the Radiation screen. Organ group chats, a heart rate album and Gut City make checking in fun. It runs as a native app on Mac, Windows and Linux with no internet connection, and all crew data in the demo is simulated.
